utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you have just said, can it be related to the incidents that took place at the OP Echo or not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Just to understand your question well, sir. Do you mean that there was a bigger plan where Echo was the trial and the whole situation was, in fact, planned? Yes, that is to my conviction, sir. I'm absolutely -- no, I'm not sure, but I'm convinced of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because when you were speaking about the incident that took place at the OP Echo, you said that the incidents were some kind of a test in terms of preparations. Did you mean to say a test or preparation for the upcoming attack? Can we interpret it that way?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: No, sir. I did not foresee an attack within four weeks on the enclave. I just analysed it as being a test case. One of the reasons I did so was that normally when you do an advance or an attack on key terrain, and OP Echo was key terrain, you keep up your momentum, you go on, as long as you don't get opponents. And after the attack on OP Echo, in fact the road to Srebrenica was open. I ordered B Company to go down there like hell with a couple of APCs to block the Serb forces off, but as you can see on the map, on that occasion, show our uniform were established and we could go down south, almost to the factory before we came to Serb forces. That's one of the reasons that I said it was not Srebrenica now, it must be a test case. But not foreseeing an attack on the enclave then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my last question, Major Franken: You compiled a list of men who were within the compound. I should like to know if you compiled that list before or after having seen the belongings of the men who had entered the white building being set on fire? Do you understand this? Did you do it before or after their belongings were burnt?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: It was before, sir. The trigger for me was the -- sorry -- increasing violence in the interrogation of the men. So I already stated that I had the feeling in the late afternoon of the 12th that we were not in control in any way anymore, and that triggered me for this solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Well, thank you very much, Major Franken. Thank you very much for coming here to testify. We understand and we share your feeling of powerlessness, of impotence, but perhaps -- and I do understand that your feelings, as a professional and as a human being, were deeply offended by what happened. But nevertheless we wish to thank you for coming here to testify about these painful events. We hope that you will regain your peace and serenity in your country here. Mr. Cayley, I believe that we have to settle the exhibits now. We have to see what to do with them. Perhaps Mr. Dubuisson could give us the numbers of these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the decision which concerns 80 and 86.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Cayley, 80, Exhibit 80 was already used, and you said that you would await another witness. I do not know whether this is the moment now, or do you still wish to wait?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, you're quite right. Exhibit 80 is the list which the previous witness referred to and which this witness provided evidential foundation for, so I would apply for that to be admitted into evidence. And Exhibit 86 is the list of the wounded in the compound, which again this witness recognised, and I would ask for that to be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Visnjic, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Therefore, 80 and 86 are admitted. Could we abuse the interpreters for another three minutes, please? Very well. The question is, indeed, whether I am or am not abusing it, but I shall nevertheless do it. We have to deliver the decision that we discussed earlier, and I have to do it now. I'd also like to seize this opportunity to say that on Friday, on Friday, we shall begin the hearing at 10.00 because the Chamber will have another business to attend to, and therefore we shall then sit as of 10.00, so that you can sleep a little longer. Yes, you can sleep a little longer. There is yet another matter, and that is that tomorrow, as I have announced, that is, a day where I shall not be able to attend, I will not be here tomorrow, and Judge Riad, being the older of the two Judges, the senior of the two Judges, will be presiding. Before we take the decision, I should like to set free Major Franken. Thank you very much for coming once again. Thank you very much. Usher, will you please help Major Franken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. The decision of the Chamber regarding the contact of parties with witnesses is as follows: A few days ago, the Defence raised a question of communication between the parties and the witnesses. According to them, the parties should no longer communicate with witnesses once the witnesses have taken the oath. The Defence did not quote a specific reason but stated that it was merely for the sake of making clear the relations of the parties to the witnesses. The Chamber was informed by the parties that they had met 25 and agreed the contact would not be prohibited between a witness and the party representing it, except after the examination-in-chief of the witness. The parties confirmed the understanding during court session but after a suggestion of the Chamber they changed their positions slightly. The Chamber believes that it should specify certain 7 points. It notes first of all that no provision of the Statute or of the Rules regulates the matter. However, it believes that the procedure followed, before this Tribunal, does not make part of any specific legal system under Rule 99a of the Rules, and that its application is to ensure the best presentation by the parties of their evidence so that the Chamber can arrive at the truth of the case submitted to it in conformity with the solemn declaration as envisaged by Rule 90b of the rules. Moreover, the Rule 98, states that the Chamber may summon witnesses whose testimony is put in evidence with a view to establishing the truth. Witnesses who appear before the Chamber, which ever party calls them – be it the Prosecution or the Defence, are no longer witnesses of one of the parties, but they are witnesses of justice. A party which calls a witness has all the possibilities of communicating with the witness before the witness takes the oath and explain the procedure, specifically all that refers to this decision. However, from the moment the witness has made the solemn declaration, this evidence may no longer have any particular link to either of the parties who may even unwittingly or subconsciously interfere with the spontaneity and the truth of the testimony as required by the spirit of the Statute and the Rules of the Tribunal. The Chamber, knows with how much care, vigilance, and neutrality, the Victims and Witnesses Unit takes care of the health, security and the well-being of witnesses. Therefore there is no need for the parties to have even for logistical reasons -- contact with any witness -- from the beginning to the end of his testimony. In view of the above , the Chamber decides in accordance with the Rules 54, 99(G) and 90(G) of the Rules, that all contact between a witness and the parties shall be prohibited as of the moment when this witness takes the solemn declaration and up to the end of his appearance before the Chamber, -- Unless under exceptional circumstances one party deems it necessary to contact a witness, this party shall then inform the Chamber prior to the contact and clearly state the reason and objective of its application. If the Chamber accepts this application, then the Chamber will also specify the conditions under which this contact may take place. This is the decision of the Chamber. We discussed it at great length and we came to this decision, which in our opinion strikes a balance between different requests and needs. And so this is the decision of the Chamber. I should like to thank the interpreters and all the personnel who were so kind as to stay a little longer so that we could give you this ruling. Therefore, tomorrow at 9.30, the Chamber will be here with Judge Riad and Judge Wald, to continue the hearing of this case. Thank you very much. Have a nice afternoon. Thank you.
